_comment: Provenance for each canonical-transcript fixture: which fields come from a REAL captured engine session vs are SYNTHETIC (schema-accurate but fabricated), and why. fixtures_test.go asserts on the REAL fields specifically, per the project's payload-assertion discipline (memory 'silent-no-op-failure-mode') — never a mere entry count. Every fixture's basename is its `engine` value, and that value must be a currently-registered internal/lm/backends name: docs/transcript.schema.json's `engine` enum IS the registry, so a fixture named for an unregistered engine cannot validate and is not coverage.

claude-code.transcript.acp.jsonl.real_source: ~/.claude/projects/-tmp-TestACPLive-ClaudeBackendDelegation1132179987-001/eeacb0c6-c962-40f8-8322-c8615ea00631.jsonl — an ACTUAL claude-code-acp structured session (internal/acp live-acceptance test fixture) recorded on this box
claude-code.transcript.acp.jsonl.real_fields: session_id, model (claude-opus-4-6), the user prompt 'Reply with exactly the single word: ping', and the assistant reply 'ping' — genuinely driven over the same ACP seam this schema targets
claude-code.transcript.acp.jsonl.synthetic: thinking entry, tool_use/tool_result pair, and the complete/token accounting (the real fixture was a minimal ping/pong with no tool call and no token footer recorded in the jsonl line captured)
claude-code.transcript.acp.jsonl.why_not_fully_real: the available real ACP-driven claude session was a bare connectivity probe; no real tool-calling claude-code-acp transcript was found on this box in this slice

mock.transcript.acp.jsonl.real_source: captured on this box by driving backends.NewMock().Chat with ChatRequest.ForwardPermissions through transcript.TeeAndClose into transcript.NewRecorder(harp, "mock") — the production structured-chat tee, not a hand-typed line
mock.transcript.acp.jsonl.real_fields: lines 5 onward: a TOOLS turn (user, thinking, tool_use, tool_result, assistant, complete) driven through the real recorder
mock.transcript.acp.jsonl.synthetic: the first turn (lines 1-4): a denial turn hand-converted from a captured permission turn when the permission kind was replaced by denied — user entry, the denied line (tool_name mock_tool, tool_call_id mock-deny-1, decider policy), the assistant reply, and the complete footer carrying the same denial
mock.transcript.acp.jsonl.why_not_fully_real: the mock is a registered, production-reachable test double (`--llm mock`); its denial turn (mock:deny) has not been re-captured through the recorder. This fixture is what exercises KindDenied.
